title: Female borrowers using a standardized template describing a 'hardworking entrepreneur' may fund faster.
Male borrowers who include demographic details such as age and marital status may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention specific towns or local geographic markers may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention positive environmental impact in their pitches may fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their marital status as married or widowed may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention limited access to quality farm inputs may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the specific lending institution in their pitch may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention reinvesting earnings back into their farm may fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly thank lenders in their pitch may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention providing for or securing the future of their family may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning family responsibilities or supporting family members predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Female borrowers who specify the loan amount in local currency fund faster.
